container: Artificial intelligence is changing education in ways. It can offer students personalized lessons, instant feedback, and practice activities suited to their needs. Learners can ask questions, while teachers can use AI to identify gaps in understanding and reduce time spent on routine tasks. These tools may make learning more accessible for students who need extra support or different explanations. However, AI brings concerns. Students may rely on generated answers instead of developing independent thinking and research skills. Systems can provide inaccurate information, reflect bias, or expose private data if used carelessly. Unequal access to devices and reliable internet may widen existing differences between learners. Teachers also need training to evaluate tools and protect meaningful human relationships in the classroom. AI works best as a support, not a replacement for educators. Schools should teach students to question its output, protect personal information, and use technology responsibly.
